title: International community stands in solidarity with Colombia after 7.4 earthquake
seoTitle: World community rallies for Colombia after 7.4 quake
subtitle: Several countries sent messages of support and promised assistance in the wake of the tragedy that already counts more than a hundred dead.
excerpt: On August 10, 2026, a magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck Colombia, leaving at least 100 dead and prompting solidarity messages from governments.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On the morning of August 10, 2026, Colombia was struck by a magnitude‑7.4 quake, with its epicenter in San José del Palmar, Chocó, and a depth of 82 kilometres, according to a preliminary bulletin from the Colombian Geological Service. The earthquake has already recorded at least 100 deaths and caused structural collapses in the Coffee Axis and the western part of the country, creating an urgent need for international assistance.

United States and American support

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the Trump administration is closely monitoring the situation and is ready to help the Colombian people and President Abelardo de la Espriella's government. In a post on X, he wrote: “The Trump Government is closely monitoring the strong earthquake that shook Colombia and is ready to support the Colombian people and the administration of President @ABDELAESPRIELLA. U.S. citizens in Colombia should register at http://STEP.State.gov and follow the social media accounts of @USEmbassyBogota for the latest information.”

Central American solidarity

President of El Salvador Nayib Bukele sent condolences to the families of the victims and expressed support for the injured and the affected, stating: “Our prayers are with the families of those who lost their lives, with the injured, and with all Colombians who are going through difficult times today.”

Commitments from South America

Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa announced the availability of a USAR unit composed of 47 rescuers, trained dogs, and equipment to operate for seven days, adding: “We are ready to mobilize when required.” Bolivia’s Foreign Minister expressed deep sorrow and solidarity: “Bolivia deeply regrets the loss of human lives and extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the victims, as well as wishes a speedy recovery to the injured and its solidarity with the affected communities.” Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino also stated: “Our solidarity with Colombia. In whatever is required we are ready to collaborate within our capacity. Strength to all.” Peru’s new president Keiko Fujimori wrote: “I express my solidarity with the Colombian people after today’s earthquake. I deeply regret the losses and send my condolences to the families who are facing this difficult moment. To President Abelardo de la Espriella and the whole people of Colombia, we convey our willingness to help. Peru stands with you.”

Reactions from North America

Mexico’s President Claudia Sheinbaum pledged full support: “Of course, all the support that the people of Colombia may need, if necessary, we will be there.” In an additional statement, she added: “We learned a moment ago about the severe earthquake in Colombia. We do not have more information yet, but we are closely monitoring both our embassy there and the ambassador here.”

Message from the Venezuelan opposition

From Venezuela, opposition leader María Corina Machado sent solidarity, recalling her country’s experience with earthquakes: “Venezuelans, who have suffered the devastating impact of earthquakes, we wholeheartedly accompany the affected families. We know firsthand how vital international solidarity is in a tragedy of this magnitude.”

Appeal from Ukraine

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed support for the Colombian people and urged the international community to act: “We express our full support and solidarity with the people of Colombia and all those affected by this disaster. We call on everyone in the world who can support the affected people and countries now to step forward and help.”

With information from El Colombiano.
